correctness.rationale: Reconstructed independent Binomial(s,p) boundary degrees, block decomposition and exact Schur complement. Independent-edge Laplacian Bernstein has summand norm <=2 and variance norm 2p(1-p)m, so its orthogonal spectrum is pm+o_P(m). Inversion yields m(bar(z)-xi)->sp(1-p)/p=s(1-p). Ordinary binomial CLT for B and Slutsky give the claimed Gaussian law and continuous threshold probability. The standalone script tests 253 deterministic brackets, 60 Schur identities and 216 random instances; it cannot replace the analytic proof. Boundaries and quantifiers are explicit.

originality.rationale: Two directly relevant full-text papers were compared theorem by theorem: Pirani and Sundaram (arXiv:1406.2271, Thm. 3) show only first-order grounded-eigenvalue concentration for fixed small sink sets; Apollonio, Tora and Vergni (arXiv:2604.00624v1, Thm. 1) develop the ecological threshold and growing-sink concentration. Neither establishes the specific fixed-s Gaussian crossover and explicit n^-1 correction. A related Tora–Vergni article was abstract-only, so historical priority remains limited; a targeted published-claim search yielded no covering claim on searched aliases.
residual_risks: Priority risk from inaccessible full text of Tora–Vergni (2026), DOI:10.1016/j.mbs.2026.109749; only abstract-level comparison is supported.

value.rationale: The critical-patch-size ecology model asks when network loss to absorbing sites overcomes local growth. A first-order sp limit cannot determine the fraction of viable random habitats at the natural 1/sqrt(n) margin. The Gaussian law answers that finite-size phase transition with exact scaling and parameter-dependent profile; the deterministic 1/n bias quantifies the ecological benefit of redistribution across the internal habitat, a physically interpretable correction distinct from binomial sampling fluctuation. The exact fixed-s setting is a natural biological boundary regime rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
